name: ASCII Table
summary: The full ASCII table in decimal, hex, octal and binary, with control code names.
about: Shows every one of the 128 standard ASCII codes, each in decimal, hexadecimal, octal, binary and its printed character, with the RFC 20 name for every control code. A filter box finds a row by any of those forms or by a control name.
supports: Each code shown in decimal, two-digit upper-case hexadecimal, three-digit octal and seven-bit binary
The RFC 20 abbreviation and name for codes 0 to 31 and for 127 (DEL), and SP for 32
The printed character itself for codes 33 to 126
Filtering by an exact number in decimal, 0x/0X hexadecimal, 0o octal or 0b binary
Filtering by a single character or by a substring of a control abbreviation or name, case-insensitively
limits: ASCII is a seven-bit code: this table stops at 127 and has nothing to say about extended 8-bit code pages such as Latin-1 or Windows-1252
The filter matches a single row per exact-number query; it does not accept a range or a comparison
Control character names are RFC 20's own abbreviations and names, not the longer definitions given in later standards
ambiguities: RFC 20 section 4.1 tags each control character's category with (CC), (FE) or (IS). Those category tags are not part of the name shown here; only the plain name is kept
Code 32 has no control abbreviation of its own in RFC 20's control-character list; it is shown here as SP (Space), matching its entry in the printable character table

standards.label: RFC 20 — ASCII format for Network Interchange
ANSI X3.4-1968 — USA Standard Code for Information Interchange

apiNotes: `ASCII_ROWS` is generated programmatically from `Array.from({ length: 128 })`, not hand-typed, so every decimal/hex/oct/bin/char column is derived arithmetically from the row's own code. `CONTROL_CODES` is a small hand-transcribed lookup keyed by code, covering 0-31, 32 (SP) and 127 (DEL); `ASCII_ROWS` reads its `abbreviation`/`name` fields from that lookup where one exists. `filterRows(query)` never mutates `ASCII_ROWS`; it returns a filtered array, and an empty query returns every row.
testNotes: RFC 20 section 4.1 is quoted directly (not copied from `CONTROL_CODES`) for at least eight control names, independently confirming the transcription. The generated decimal/hex/oct/bin columns are checked against `Number.prototype.toString` conversions computed in the test, not against `ASCII_ROWS` itself, so a generation bug cannot hide behind a self-referential assertion.
